title: Forbruksartikler til renhold og kantinedrift
description: Bakgrunn og formål Vestfold fylkeskommune har i dag en rammeavtale for kjøp av renholds-, papir-, plast- og storkjøkkenprodukter. Avtalen har sluttdato i januar 2027, og det er derfor behov for å gjennomføre en ny anskaffelse for å etablere en ny rammeavtale fra samme tidspunkt. Anskaffelsen skal dekke fylkeskommunens løpende behov for varer og tilhørende tjenester til renhold og kantinedrift ved videregående skoler, tannklinikker, museer og fylkeshuset. Formålet er å sikre stabil forsyning, effektiv drift og lik kvalitet over tid på tvers av lokasjoner. Det er samtidig et mål at den nye rammeavtalen legger til rette for et hensiktsmessig standardsortiment med nødvendige lokale tilpasninger, god sortimentsstyring og en brukervennlig bestillingsløsning. Fylkeskommunen ønsker også produkter og emballasjeløsninger med bedre miljøegenskaper, samt sikker kompatibilitet mellom forbruksartikler, dispensere og maskiner. Produktgrupper det er behov for er: Avfallshåndtering Hygieneprodukter Kantineprodukter Renoldsmidler Renholdsprodukter Tørkepapir

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Purchase Order to London Stock Exchange Group
description: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) intends to award a fixed-price purchase order on a single source basis to London Stock Exchange Group, PLC; 10 Paternoster Square, London, ED4M 7LS, United Kingdom for online access to Stock Exchange Daily Official List (SEDOL) data. The NAICS code is 518210. The contracting officer has determined that London Stock Exchange Group, PLC is the only source that can reasonably meet the SEC�s requirement in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. The SEDOL Masterfile contains unique identifiers assigned to securities in the United Kingdom and Ireland. These identifiers are in use in data sets from other vendors, from whom the numbers are downloaded for use on the SEC services. The London Stock Exchange Group is the only source identified that can meet the SEC�s requirement. The period of performance for the purchase order is one base year and one option year. The total estimated value of this purchase order is under the Simplified Acquisition Threshhold. This notice is not a competitive request for proposals. A competitive solicitation will not be issued. Interested parties who believe they can provide these services may submit a capabilities statement to the Contracting Officer, Flanice Lewis, lewisf@sec.gov, no later than November 27, 2026, at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Responses must be submitted via email. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

Fabrication of a Replacement Stilling Well Platform and Associated Components for the Pointe-des-Cascades Hydrometric Station (02MC005), Fleuve Saint-Laurent, Québec
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) is seeking a fixed price quote for construction services to complete the fabrication of a steel platform for a new stilling well installation at the hydrometric station identified as 02MC005 Saint Laurent (Fleuve) à Pointe-des-Cascades located in Pointe-des-Cascades near Montréal, Québec. The installation and decommissioning components of the project have been included as optional deliverables. This project work is associated with a life cycle replacement of the stilling well which is no longer functioning due to rust out. The new stilling well will improve the accuracy of water level monitoring on the St. Lawrence River and allow for safe and efficient operation of the hydrometric station. The objective of this project is for the Contractor to fabricate a hot-dip galvanized steel grated platform and associated components in accordance with the drawing package provided in Appendix B. The installation of the platform, stilling well, and other project components (listed below) are optional work, which may only be exercised through a contract amendment before the expiry of the contract. The requirement is subject to the provisions of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA). The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

The principal geographic area covered by this contract encompasses NAVFAC Atlantic's AOR, NAVFAC Pacific�s AOR and the adjacent waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans, including the Continental United States, the Caribbean, Europe, and North Africa. Examples of taskings required to complete this work may include analysis of port facility and infrastructure construction, renovation, and/or demolition; dredging; base realignment and closure (BRAC) actions; and proposed operational actions related to ship homeporting, waterfront activities and manned and unmanned asset activities. title: Intent to Sole Source - Type-C A&E Services for Construction of SFS Facility
description: The 145th Mission Support Group Contracting office in Charlotte, NC intends to issue a written request for proposal and resulting firm-fixed price sole source award to AECOM. This sole source award will be for Type �C� services for construction contract administration for the Construction of the Security Forces Building project. Type �C� services include but are not limited to documenting and providing answers to contractor�s requests for information, submittal reviews, attendance and records at progress meetings, review of lab results, preparation of as-built drawings, and multiple site visits to inspect the building during construction. This requirement is a follow-on award to AECOM. The requirement was previously negotiated and awarded via task order W50S87-21-F-5013. That award included Type A and B services for the design of the Construction of the Security Forces Building project. Type A services included the basis of design (specifically the design intent), the development of the project concept, and associated site investigations. The Type B services included the design narrative and the development of the construction documents. Because AECOM designed and certified the drawings and specifications and is liable for the quality of their design, it is economical and efficient to award the Type C services as a sole source follow-on contract. There is tremendous performance and liability risk associated with another A-E firm taking over the Type C services for a project that was designed by a different firm. Having the original designer, AECOM, on contract to perform the construction phase services is necessary for the Government to ensure responsibility for their design, including ensuring the design is constructible, maintainable and operable, that the project documentation is clear, sufficiently detailed, accurate and coordinated, and contains minimal errors. An award to a new A-E other than AECOM would increase the risk associated with these issues and potentially affect the Government�s rights under FAR 52.236-23, Responsibility of the Architect-Engineer Contractor, if another A-E were to represent or attempt to revise the current drawings and/or specifications. This clause states that the �Contractor shall be responsible for the professional quality, technical accuracy, and the coordination of all designs, drawings, specifications, and other services furnished by the Contractor�. However, if a new A-E were to make recommendations during the Type C services to revise or deviate from the original drawings or specifications, any liability resulting from those changes could not be attributed to the original A-E. This could potentially create a dangerous and complicated scenario if the Government needed to hold the responsible A-E party liable for any errors or deficiencies in the designs, drawings, and/or specifications. This action is being taken using the authority of 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.

title: Grand Jury Court Reporting Services - United States Attorney's Office, District of Wyoming
description: Amendment 1: Responses to Industry Question and Updated SOW. Solicitation Number: 15JA0527Q00000004 The Executive Office for United States Attorneys (EOUSA), on behalf of the United States Attorney�s Office for the District of Wyoming (USAO?WY), anticipates making a single award for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Grand Jury court reporting services by location; however, EOUSA reserves the right to make multiple awards if deemed in the Government�s best interest. Offerors may submit a quote for either or both of the two locations�Cheyenne and Casper�and must clearly specify which location(s) they intend to serve. The resulting IDIQ contract(s) will support USAO?WY in carrying out the mission of the United States Attorneys, who serve as the nation�s principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General. The anticipated award date is February 1, 2027. The ordering period will be one (1) base year period with four (4) option year periods. This requirement is a 100% small business set-aside. The award will be made under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 561492, Court Reporting and Stenotype Services, with a small business size standard of $19.5M in average annual receipts. All task orders awarded under this IDIQ will be T&M and will comply with FAR 16.505, ordering procedures. The Contractor shall provide the labor, supervision, and transportation necessary to provide the court reporting services as described in the Solicitation. Interest parties are advised that this solicitation includes the provision FAR 52.204-7 System for Award Management (SAM) which requires than an Offeror be registered in SAM when submitting a quote and continues to be registered throughout the duration of the contract. Quoters shall include a cover page or complete the SF1449 that includes their Unique Entity ID (UEI) and Tax Identification Number (TIN). For additional information, please call 866-606-8220 or visit the SAM website at https://www.sam.gov/. The Contracting Officer will verify registration in the SAM database prior to award by entering the potential awardees UEI into the SAM database. Background Investigations: Minimum Security Clearance Requirements for Contractor Personnel. All Contractor personnel who will have access to Grand Jury material must pass the basic security clearance requirements set forth in Contract Clause EOUSA-AI-10-1E Federal Grand Jury Court Reporting Security Requirements prior to starting work on-site. Security requirements and forms are described in Local Clause AI-10-F, Security Requirements for Classified Contract (May 2016). Additionally, the elevated following court-specific background investigation levels must also be obtained and maintained throughout performance by Contractor personnel: a. title: U.S. Mission Burundi Local Guard Program
description: The Department of State is conducting market research to determine the degree of interest and capability by all business sizes (small and large) in providing local guard services at the U.S. Embassy Bujumbura, Burundi. The Department of State, Bureau of Diplomatic Security plays an essential role in ensuring that foreign policy missions are accomplished in a safe and secure environment. The primary mission of the local guard service is to provide protection for United States personnel, facilities, and equipment from damage or loss due to violent attack and theft. The local guard services shall prevent unauthorized access; protect life; maintain order; deter criminal and terrorist attacks against employees, dependents, and property; and prevent damage to all U.S. assets. The NAICS code for these services is 561612. Responses must clearly demonstrate capabilities through examples of previous and/or current guard security contracts or experience closely related thereto. Vendors must specifically address the following capabilities: Current licenses, work authorizations in compliance with host country law required for the execution of work, including firearms permits and licenses. Licenses must be in the name of the U.S. business. Knowledge of and compliance with host country labor law which may require bonuses, specific minimum wage levels, premium pay for holidays, payments for social security, pensions, severance pay, sick or health benefits, childcare or any other benefit Knowledge of and compliance with host country tax law Ability to provide all types of insurance coverage required by host country in performance of services, such as automobile liability, comprehensive general liability, worker�s compensation, employer�s liability, etc. Furnishing, operating, and maintaining a radio network, including acquiring all licenses and permits that may be required for frequencies and the operation of all communications equipment Familiarity or experience with associated security equipment such as Guard Electronic Monitoring System (GEMS), Central Alarm Monitoring systems (CAMS), closed-circuit television systems, x-ray and explosive detection equipment Furnishing guard force equipment such as uniforms, vehicles, and weapons Ability to overcome language barriers Capability of instructing, providing, and qualifying personnel in the use of firearms, as well as x-ray equipment and radio equipment, including obtaining the access to a firearm training facility Ability to maintain a guard staff on a 24 hour 7 day a week basis with the ability to immediately backfill vacant positions due to resignations, rotations and illnesses due to a variety of reasons such as flu and food poisoning Capability of dealing with organized actions by direct labor personnel such as strikes (anticipated and unanticipated) and labor unrest (work slowdowns and/or organized failure of employees to report for shift changes) Ability to hire and train, including English language training and weapons training, if required, a guard staff consisting of host country nationals Ability to provide trained equipment technicians for all vehicles, radios and weapons required in the performance of the contract Ability to train a sizeable workforce to adapt quickly to unfamiliar laws and customs as well as the ability of company officials to gain quickly information regarding the laws and customs needed to maintain and equip such a workforce Experience or capability of getting contractor-furnished equipment and goods through customs and/or similar governmental agencies of the host country Understanding import and export regulations Understanding and familiarity of the Arms Export Control Act (AECA) and International Traffic in Arms Regulation (ITAR) and the capability of complying with both by the performance date of any contract awarded requiring the execution of this Statute (22 U.S.C. 2778-2780) Managing smooth contract transition efforts. Ability to safely keep and track Government-Furnished Property Ability to screen personnel to meet suitability requirements for guard force positions Strong skill in instant, situational decision-making, e.g., response to threats Organized billing and invoicing procedures It is requested that all interested parties submit their capabilities by e-mail to Brian Averhart at AverhartB@state.gov addressing each of the above requirements by 12:00 EST, 27 November 2026. Interested parties shall also complete the attached Contractor Information Sheet. If you have any questions or comments, please reference this Sources Sought Notice when emailing. description: This is a Notice of Intent, not a request for proposal. The National Institute of Health, Clinical Center (NIH-CC) intends to negotiate on an other than full and open competition basis with the following vendor: Illumina, Inc. Acquisition Description: The purpose of this acquisition is to purchase two Illumina MiSeq i100 series instruments. These instruments will be used by the NIH HLA Laboratory to produce high resolution HLA typing results for the numerous transplant protocols supported by the laboratory. It will replace the current Illumina MiSeq instruments in the lab that were purchased in 2021 and 2022. The vendor will discontinue service on the current model of the MiSeq. New instruments are required to ensure time to validate these replacements before discontinuation of service. The total dollar value for this order is $139,100.52. The MiSeq is an integrated instrument that performs clonal amplification, genomic DNA sequencing, and data analysis with base calling, alignment, variant calling, and reporting in a single run. The MiSeq provides the Lab with the highest HLA typing results possible. The transplant protocols served by the HLA Lab require highest resolution possible to increase the chance of a successful transplant. The HLA Lab currently owns two MiSeq instruments, so the procedures and Quality Control assessments are in place. The order aims to replace the Illumina Miseq � s/n M07700 (property ID is 02223449) and s/n M08636 (property ID is 02268689) that were purchased in 2019 and 2022. Replacement is necessary to ensure proper performance of these instruments prior to discontinuation of service for the current model of the Illumina MiSeq instruments by the vendor. title: Z2DA--666-27-102 Lightning Protection Update B71N
description: GENERAL: Introduction: An inspection for current code compliance of the lightning Protection System on Building 71N has been conducted and found the system needs upgrades and repairs to meet current NFPA 780 and UL96A standards. The Sheridan VA Medical Center needs the services of a qualified contractor to perform the needed lightning protection upgrades to the main hospital building 71N. Located on the Sheridan Wyoming Veterans Affairs Medical Center (VAMC) campus, at 1898 Fort Road, Sheridan, Wyoming 82801. Statement of Work: Specifics a. Existing Conditions The existing lightning protection system (LPS) for Building 71N was installed in 1989 during the building s original construction. Overall, the system remains in fair condition, though it requires repair because several air terminals have become detached from their adhesive bonds to the roof surface. Air terminals are present at all high points of the structure, and all roof-mounted equipment and appurtenances are properly grounded. A main grounding bus connects the communication systems and possibly the electrical distribution system to the primary service ground. The specific location where the grounding system bonds together the structural steel, electrical system, lightning protection components, and plumbing to create an equipotential ground could not be identified during the assessment. A continuous grounding loop encircles Buildings 9, 71, and 71N, with all roof air terminals and down conductors tied into this loop. Down conductors descend to the loop at the corners of each of these buildings. Each air terminal has at least two separate grounding paths, satisfying current code requirements. No Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices were observed in the system. The lower 8 feet of the ground down conductors are encased in PVC electrical conduit for protection. New Construction Recent construction has added large equipment and a screen wall to the roof, which now obstructs and interferes with the original positioning of the existing air terminals. This new equipment sits higher than the existing lightning protection system components, rendering the current air terminals ineffective at intercepting and safely directing lightning strikes to ground. Project Requirements To bring the existing lightning protection system (LPS) into compliance the following corrections are needed: Install Transient Voltage Surge Suppression (TVSS) devices at the building s main service panel. Establish proper bonding by interconnecting all electrical systems, communication systems, piping, and structural steel at the service entrance to create an equipotential ground. Repair all roof air terminals that have detached or pulled away from their adhesive mounts on the roof surface. Install new air terminals at both ends of each screen wall, with additional terminals spaced at 20-foot intervals along the top of each wall, and at the highest point of the HVAC ductwork. Install an air terminal at each corner of the new HVAC equipment. Connect all newly installed air terminals to the existing LPS using #2 bare copper conductors. After these corrections have been completed, a qualified inspection is required to verify full compliance with NFPA 780 and UL 96A standards. Upon successful inspection, a Master Label Certificate should be issued for the lightning protection system. General: Construction project is to be completed within 120 calendar days from date of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractor shall provide all equipment, materials, supplies, tools, software, supervision, and labor required for this project, which may include, but is not limited to, demolition work, providing negative pressure environment for work, and providing all new equipment, utilities, and room finishes as indicated in the plans and this SOW per VA construction standards. Safety submittals shall be completed and approved prior to the commencement of on-site construction work. Material selection submittals shall be completed and approved prior to ordering of materials for the project. The building tenants not in the construction areas will remain at work in the buildings during this construction. Patients will remain on the floor in areas not under construction, so the contractor shall make patient safety, and infection control measures a priority. The contractor shall coordinate work locations and schedules with VA COR to minimize impact to building tenants. All electrical, carpentry, architectural, mechanical work, product design, project management, and other work needed on this project shall be provided by the Contractor. All required electrical work, low, medium, or high voltage, shall be installed and terminated by the Contractor. No wiring or cabling shall be abandoned in place. All piping, cabling, and wiring shall be labeled. All cabling and patch cabling shall match the VAMC s station-standard colors. The installation must, at a minimum, be in accordance with all applicable codes indicated in the Department of Veterans Affairs Design Manuals and VA .PUBLICATIONS (Master Construction Specifications, Construction Standards, National Fire Protection Association (NFPA), Underwriters Laboratory (UL), International Building Code IBC 2003, and National Electric Code (NEC) building codes and standards and the VA Information Security Handbook 6500.6, 6550.0 etc.). The Contractor shall read and be familiar with the most current editions of the applicable codes, standards, guides, and manuals. Sources can be accessed at the Office of Construction and Facilities Management s Technical Information Library (TIL) (http://www.cfm.va.gov/TIL). Any penetrations through any floors, ceilings, or walls shall be fire caulked, or otherwise fire sealed, and shall be done in this contract to meet VA standards and NFPA standards. Contractor shall utilize the VAMC s station-standard fire stop products or approved equal product(s). The station-standard products are SpecSeal fire caulk product is SpecSeal SSS Intumescent Firestop Sealant; and, if needed, the SpecSeal Composite Sheet may be used in areas approved by the COR. The Contractor shall inquire of the COR if any existing equipment, fixtures, hardware, doors, frames, or any other property removed is desired to be retained by the VA for reuse elsewhere within the medical center, at the time of removal. If the VA desires to retain an item, the Contractor shall deliver it to a location designated by the COR. If the VA does not desire to retain an item, the Contractor shall dispose of it properly off-station. The new components installed shall be tested and commissioned, re-certified, and/or tested before VA acceptance. All testing parameters shall be provided by the Contractor with source references to the COR and 3rd-party reviewer before testing begins. Copies of all test reports must be provided to the COR. HVAC systems that have changes made to them as part of this project, beyond diffuser replacement, shall be tested and balanced by the Contractor. Any IT data cables installed or modified as part of this effort shall be tested after installation. Test methods and plans shall be coordinated with the COR. Any Med Gas systems modified as part of this effort shall be re-certified back to the closest shut-off in the system. The Contractor shall arrange for any required re-certification as part of this contract and shall provide plans and results to the COR for approval. Fire alarm devices that are tied into the building fire alarm system, that are replaced or relocated as a result of this work, shall be tested before that phase of the project is complete. The Contractor shall arrange for all required fire alarm testing. If a building s fire alarm system is under warranty, testing must be accomplished by the contractor who holds the warranty. Any fire sprinklers that are relocated as part of this project shall be reviewed and approved by VA Safety prior to installation. All fire sprinkler work shal

description: La présente consultation a pour objet la mise en place d’un accord-cadre à bons de commandes, mono-attributaire, sans montant minimum et un montant maximum de 5 000 000 €HT, pour des prestations de locations de véhicules de tourisme et utilitaires en courte et moyenne durées. L’accord cadre est conclu pour une durée maximale de Quarante-Huit (48) mois. La démarche s’applique à l’ensemble des divisions et Business Units de l’EPIC (Etablissement Public à caractère Industriel et Commercial) et les filiales de la Ratp. Le périmètre géographique des prises de location est limité au territoire français (métropolitain), avec de possibles usages transfrontaliers. Les prestations sont définis par des locations courte durée (LCD) et moyenne durée (LMD) de véhicules particuliers et utilitaires sans chauffeur au profit des entités bénéficiaires du Groupe RATP. Les prestations concernent notamment : • Une offre professionnelle portant sur la mise à disposition de véhicules particuliers et utilitaires, • Une offre dite Loisirs, à destination des salariés du Groupe pour leurs besoins personnels. Les principales prestations attendues sont les suivantes : • Prestations de locations de véhicules de tourisme et utilitaire en courte et moyenne durée, • Mise à disposition d'un outil de réservation en ligne / site dédié pour les locations à titre personnel, • Mise à disposition des tarifs négociés dans l'outil de réservation en ligne de l'agence de voyages de la RATP, • Information, conseil et assistance auprès des différents utilisateurs du groupe RATP tout au long de la prestation de location. Pour les besoins du présent marché, la location courte durée (LCD) correspond à une durée inférieure ou égale à 30 jours calendaires consécutifs. La location moyenne durée (LMD) correspond à une durée comprise entre 31 jours et 12 mois. Afin de répondre aux différents besoins des bénéficiaires du marché, le titulaire devra proposer des offres accessibles au moyen de plusieurs canaux de réservation distincts : - Via l’agence de voyage désignée par le groupe RATP - Via une plateforme de réservation dédiée aux professionnels - Via une interface dédiée pour l’offre dite « Loisirs » Pour chacun de ces canaux, le titulaire décrira précisément les modalités d’accès, de réservation, de modification et d’annulation, ainsi que les conditions tarifaires, les moyens de paiement, les règles de validation et les prestations associées. Le titulaire veillera à assurer une présentation claire et cohérente des catégories de véhicules disponibles. Les correspondances entre les catégories commerciales proposées sur chaque canal et la classification ACRISS/SIPP devront être précisées dans son offre. À titre indicatif, le nombre de jour de location annuel est estimé à environ 33 620 et les dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durées sur l’année 2025 sont réparties entre véhicules utilitaires pour 55% et véhicules particuliers pour 45%, environ. La répartition estimée des dépenses par canal de réservation est la suivante : - Via l’agence de voyage désignée par le groupe RATP : 20 % du volume de dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durée sur l’année 2025, - Via une plateforme de réservation dédiée aux professionnels : 80 % du volume de dépenses en location de courte et moyenne durée sur l’année 2025. Cette évaluation est donnée à titre indicative et pourra évoluer en fonction des circonstances conjoncturelles du marché et ne constitue pas un engagement ferme de commande de la part du groupe RATP.

title: Z2DA--523A4-CSI-288 3.0T MRI Site Prep - Design Build West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC_ West Roxbury, MA
description: Page 1 of 1 INTRODUCTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single Firm-Fixed-Price contract for the design-build (DB) project #523A4-CSI-288 West Roxbury VA Medical Center located in West Roxbury, MA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach. The anticipated solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Parts 36 and 15, considering Technical and Price Factors. This project requires comprehensive design-build services for the the 3T MRI Site Preparation Design Build project at the West Roxbury VA Medical Center (VAMC) located in West Roxbury, MA. This project will provide construction of a temporary mobile Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) suite as well as all utility services and finishes necessary in the designated locations to allow for the installation of an MRI system by the Equipment Contractor. The work shall include, but not limited to, all labor, transportation, materials, apparatus, tools, equipment and permits necessary to provide for the renovation of the rooms, removal of the existing equipment, flooring, ceiling, sinks, casework, doors, shielding and installation of new flooring, ceiling, casework, doors, sinks, lighting, painting, med gas, shielding divider and relocation of electrical and HVAC work. Work to be performed at VAMC West Roxbury in accordance with the Statement of Work, Specifications, Drawings, Federal, State, and Local Codes. Strict noise and infection control measures shall be always followed. Off-hours and weekend work may be required to complete contractual requirements due to the location and sensitivity of the patient population. Existing life safety systems within Building 1 shall not be impaired at any time during the performance of the work. ADMINISTRATIVE: The anticipated solicitation will be issued as an RFP in accordance with FAR Part 36.3 Two Phase Design Build Selection Procedures and FAR Part 15 Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation will be advertised as an SDVOSB set-aside. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45 million. The solicitation is anticipated to be issued in early November 2026. The period of performance is approximately 430 calendar days from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $2,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to the CS and CO: Dawn.Schydzik@va.gov and William.Henkel@VA.gov . Telephone calls will not be accepted. -END-

The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potentials of a Base Support, Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Performance-Based contract with non-recurring services to perform Regional Fire Trucks Maintenance and Repair at the Norfolk Naval Shipyard, Portsmouth, VA, Norfolk Naval Station Norfolk, VA, Joint Expeditionary Base Little Creek, Naval Air Station Oceana, Virginia Beach, VA, Dam Neck Fleet Training Center, Virginia Beach, VA, Yorktown Naval Weapons Station Yorktown, VA, Cheatham Annex, Williamsburg, VA, Fort Story and other Areas of Responsibility (AOR). General Work Requirements: 1700000 C � Base Support Vehicles and Equipment The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary for the following: The intent of Annex 1700000 Base Support Vehicles and Equipment is to specify the requirements for the operation, certification, inspection, repair, trucking, towing, testing, and maintenance of Emergency Fire Trucks and Vehicles. The work identified is to be provided by means of a Base Support, Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with non-recurring work. Source Selection procedures will be used to evaluate and select the proposal that provides the lowest price and is technically acceptable to the Government. Offerors will be evaluated using the Lowest Prices Technically Acceptable (LPTA) Method. In order to permit efficient competition, the Navy will utilize the following methodology: Proposals will initially be screened for price and placed in order of price (lowest price to highest price). The Navy will then evaluate the non-price factors of the lowest priced proposal. The Navy will award to the Lowest Priced Technically Acceptable proposal. However, if the lowest priced proposal is not found to be technically acceptable, the Navy, at its sole discretion, reserves the right to increase the number of proposals it will review, until the Government identifies a technically acceptable proposal. Accordingly, under this methodology, the non-price factors of some proposals may not be evaluated by the Navy. If discussions are deemed necessary by the Contracting Officer, all proposals will be evaluated (both non-price and price) for the purpose of establishing a competitive range. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposals (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The Offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Technical Approach/Management, Factor 2 � Corporate Experience, Factor 3 � Safety and Factor 4 � Past Performance. NOTE: Offerors MUST be evaluated as technically ACCEPTABLE under Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order to be considered technically acceptable overall. For Factor 2 Corporate Experience and Factor 4 Past Performance: The offeror shall submit projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity to the solicitation. Size/Scope/Complexity: Experience providing all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide Fire Trucks Maintenance and Repair Services as defined in the RFP. The Offeror shall demonstrate the required experience totaling at least $500,000.00, either on one contract or collectively over multiple contracts/task orders , over the past five years. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period with four (4), one-year option periods, and one (1), six-month option period which, cumulatively, will not exceed sixty-six (66) months. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potentials of a Firm Fixed Price (FFP)/Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Performance-Based contract with recurring and non-recurring services to perform Regional Fire Trucks Maintenance and Repair Services in support of the Hampton Roads Areas of Responsibility (AOR). General Work Requirements: 1700000 C Base Support Vehicles and Equipment The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment, facilities, transportation, incidental engineering and other items necessary to provide the services outlined and described in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). Source Selection procedures will be used to select the proposal that provides the lowest price and is technically acceptable to the Government. Offerors will be evaluated using the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) Method. In order to permit efficient competition, the Navy will utilize the following methodology: Proposals will initially be screened for price and placed in order of price (lowest price to highest price). The Navy will then evaluate the non-price factors of the lowest priced proposal. The Navy will award to the Lowest Priced Technically Acceptable proposal. However, if the lowest priced proposal is not found to be technically acceptable, the Navy, at its sole discretion, reserves the right to increase the number of proposals it will review, until the Government identifies a technically acceptable proposal. Accordingly, under this methodology, the non-price factors of some proposals may not be evaluated by the Navy. If discussions are deemed necessary by the Contracting Officer, all proposals will be evaluated (both non-price and price) for the purpose of establishing a competitive range. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposals (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The Offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Technical Approach/Management, Factor 2 � Corporate Experience, Factor 3 � Safety and Factor 4 � Past Performance. NOTE: Offerors MUST be evaluated as technically ACCEPTABLE under Factors 1, 2, 3 and 4 in order to be considered technically acceptable overall. For Factor 2 Corporate Experience and Factor 4 Past Performance: The offeror shall submit projects that are similar in size, scope and complexity to the solicitation. Size: A contract with a yearly value of at least $100,000.00 for recurring services. Scope: Offeror must have provided all labor, supervision, management, tools, materials, equipment facilities, transportation, incidental, engineering and other items required to perform Base Support Vehicles and Equipment services as described in the Performance Work Statement (PWS). Complexity: Offeror must have been responsible for responding simultaneously to service orders for several customers or installations. Offers shall be submitted for the performance of work for a period of one year. However, the initial term of the contract may be for a period of less than one year. The Government has the option to extend the term of the contract services for additional periods of one to twelve months. The contract will be for a base period with four (4) one-year option periods, and one (1) six (6) month option period which, cumulatively, will not exceed sixty-six (66) months. The proposed procurement will be issued as a NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic Electronic Contract with online ordering capability using FedMall for the Non-Recurring Exhibit Line Item Numbers (ELINs). Acceptance of Government Purchase Credit Cards is required along with the purchase of FedMall Encrypted software. The North American Classification System (NAICS) for this procurement is 811111; the size standard is $9.0 million. The proposed procurement listed herein is a �Full and Open/Unrestricted� Competitive procurement. The RFP will be made available in electronic format only (Adobe Acrobat (.pdf)) and will be posted on the SAM.gov website around 02 Dec 2026. The estimated proposal due date shall be at least 30 days after the RFP is posted. INTRODUCTION: The USACE, NAN, is conducting market research to identify capable and interested contractors to provide Construction Management Services within the CONUS Area of Responsibility (AOR). Specifically, this market survey is being conducted to determine if there is an adequate number of qualified firms capable of performing the required work in the specified locations. If your firm is interested, possesses a record of successful past performance on similar requirements, and has the capacity to fulfill the scope of work outlined below, you are highly encouraged to submit a response. Weekly coordination meetings on non-design-related issues (quality, safety, schedule, contract admin). CMS (import/export, Quality Control System (QCS) training, etc.). Request for information (RFI) response to contractor requests for routine clarifications on contract requirements (not design clarifications). Review of operation and maintenance (O&M) manuals. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION/ SOURCES SOUGHT � Manufacturing of Machined and Composite Parts, along with Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing)
description: Issue Date: 12 November 2026 Closing Date: 27 November 2026 - 2:00 PM ET This notification is connected to previous synopsis and solicitation N0016423RWS68. The purpose of this Request For Information (RFI) is to notify industry of the Government�s intent to announce a forthcoming solicitation via the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) module. The announcement will involve rolling admission potential to award additional MAC Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contracts to Small Business Concerns, as well as a possible ceiling increase from $30M to $120M due to emergent requirements. The Statement of Work (SOW) and scope of the requirement remains unchanged, with the original SOW attached to this RFI for reference. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT - The Government is issuing this RFI/SS announcement as part of a market research effort on behalf of Crane Division, Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC Crane) and is seeking information for market research purposes relative to capabilities available to support the manufacturing of Machine and Composite Parts, along with Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing). These manufacturing efforts will support components related to EA18G Growler and P-8A Poseidon aircraft, as well as various other related platforms. The purpose and objective of this announcement is to find highly qualified fabrication facilities with expertise in the following areas: Precision machining operations such as sawing, grinding, turning, and milling of both metallic and non-metallic materials Welding, fabrication, and assembly of metallic and non-metallic materials and components to produce completed assemblies in accordance with drawings or 3-D models and within the defined tolerances Other various machine shop services including, but not limited to, water jet cutting, plasma & laser cutting, hot and cold forming, tool & die fabrication, as well as inspection & certification. Composite capabilities such as autoclave operations, prepreg and wet lay-up operations, grinding, sanding, patching/repair work, debulking, testing, and certification of materials and adhesives. Additive Manufacturing capabilities that include 3D printing of various polymer and metal components, and the ability to document the process. Interested parties are strongly encouraged to submit an initial synopsis (commonly referred to as �white paper�. This white paper should not exceed 20 pages written (Times New Roman, 12 font) or MS PowerPoint slides, (excluding supporting information such as commercial literature, catalogues, manuals, vendor�s current equipment list, responses to Government�s market research questions, etc.), with an executive summary (one page or less) on their capabilities. A draft Statement of Work is provided as an Attachment to aid interested sources in understanding the scope of work that may be executed under this potential procurement. Contractors must be properly registered in the Government System for Award Management database (SAM). Contractors may obtain information on SAM registration and annual confirmation of requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220, or via the Internet at www.sam.gov. This announcement does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation or ultimately award a contract. The U. S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement will NOT be reimbursed. Any information provided that is marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosures to non-government personnel and entities. The Government may elect to visit, or host a visit, from any potential sources following the market survey. Your interest in this program is appreciated. Responses from Small and Small Disadvantaged Business firms are highly encouraged. Firms responding should indicate if they are a small business, a socially and economically disadvantaged business, 8(a) firms, historically black colleges or universities, and minority institutions. Responses to the RFI shall include the following: Submitter's Name Street Address, City, State, nine (9) digit Zip Code Point of Contact (POC) POC Telephone and facsimile numbers Announcement Number: N0016427SNC15 Unique Entity Identification number Current CMMC level in accordance with 252.204-7025 Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements White papers and/or any associated questions may be submitted any time prior to expiration of this announcement, but shall be received by the Government no later than the closing date and time 27 November 2026 at 2:00PM ET. Respondents are solely responsible for properly marking and clearly identifying any proprietary information or trade secrets contained within their responses. The Government will not be liable, or suffer any consequential damages, for any proprietary information not properly marked and clearly identified. Proprietary information received in response to this RFI/SS will be safeguarded and handled in accordance with applicable Government regulations. In addition, if responses include technical requirements that have been identified as CUI in accordance with NIST SP 800-171, the documents shall be identified with the appropriate category markings. See https://www.archives.gov/cui/registry/category-marking-list for guidance. All information received in response to this notice that is marked proprietary will be handled accordingly. NSWC Crane makes no implied or in fact contracts by issuing this RFI. Acknowledgement of receipt of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified of the NSWC Crane�s view of the information received. Do not send any material that requires a non-disclosure agreement or identify information that is business sensitive. Responses to this notice will not be returned. All information provided becomes U.S. Navy property and will not be returned. Your interest in this response is appreciated. Electronic submissions only, no hard copy submissions will be accepted. Electronic submissions regarding this announcement may be directed to Ms. Shannon Reinhart, Phone: (812) 381-7166, E-mail: shannon.l.reinhart.civ@us.navy.mil. Please refer to announcement number N0016427SNC15 in all correspondence and communication.

description: ********** SOURCES SOUGHT TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION AND MARKET SURVEY FOR LARGE-SCALE CIVIL WORKS CONSTRUCTION ********** ********** INTRODUCTION ********** ********** The United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement for Thomas J O Brien Lock and Dam Major Rehabilitation - Construction, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. O Brien Lock and Controlling Works Major Rehabilitation project on the Calumet River in Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. The facility features a 110 ft by 1,000 ft lock chamber with concrete-capped circular sheet pile cells and low-lift sector gates regulating water exchange between Lake Michigan and the inland waterway network. description: THE INTENT OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS TO IDENTIFY QUALIFIED SMALL BUSINESSES, specifically 8(a), HUBZone, woman-owned, and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, for the requirement described below. The intent of this Sources Sought is to identify capable small business that can perform with limitations on subcontracting. The scope of work provides all personnel, equipment, containers, tools, materials, supervision, and other items or services necessary to perform de-manufacturing (DEMAN) operations. The Contractor shall meet the standards including disposal and recycling as defined in this Performance Work Statement for Defense Logistics Agency Disposition Services (DLA DS) site located at Gimcheon, South Korea. DLA DS disposes of foreign excess personal property of the United States Department of War (U.S. DoW). DLA DS receives property that is no longer required for use in the DoW and decides whether the property is usable or scrap. If usable property is not needed for redistribution within the Federal U.S. Government, it may be donated to state and local U.S. Governments, sold to the public, or processed for recovery of specific metals and materials required for use by the DoW. Only material that has not been disposed of by these outlets or is determined to be scrap shall be subject to this contract. title: Solicitation: Construct Combat Rescue Helicopter Flight Simulator Facility at Moffett ANGB
description: The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, to include all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances, and supervision necessary for the construction of a Combat Rescue Helicopter (CRH) Operational Flight Trainer (OFT) simulator facility at Moffett Air National Guard Base (ANGB), Mountain View, California. This project will provide an approximately 8,202 gross square foot building consisting of a multi-story, high bay area to house the CRH-OFT simulator, with a single-story area containing CRH mission planning, briefing and debriefing rooms, administrative areas for training and support staff, OFT maintenance and parts storage rooms, secure and non-secure telecommunication rooms, latrine facilities and mechanical, electrical and utility support rooms utilizing conventional design and construction. The building will be of permanent construction with electrical, mechanical, HVAC, plumbing, wet sprinkler fire suppression, fire detection, access control, direct digital control, and utility management. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Air space and insulation to be located inside the cavity wall to meet Energy Code requirements. The primary roofing materials will be standing seam metal roofing to match other installation facilities and the perimeter sloped roof design will include a prefinished standing seam metal roof panel system over rigid insulation. The exterior walls will be constructed with cavity wall construction including interior non-load bearing metal studs (or CMU wall backup at Simulator Bay) with gypsum board and exterior CMU veneer and metal panel. Main entrance doors will be a pair of anodized aluminum storefront entrance doors with insulating glass including a sidelight. The Mechanical, Electrical, Sim Bay and secondary egress doors will be painted, insulated hollow metal door and frames with controlled access. Antiterrorism/Force Protection elements are incorporated. Supporting facilities include landscaping, utilities, pavements, storm drainage, sanitary sewer, site improvements, communications support, cybersecurity control systems, and tempest security.

The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Modernized Airborne Radio Control Head MARCH / Control Head Unit (CHU)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), on behalf of the Product Manager, Aviation Mission Systems Architecture (PM AMSA), intends to award a sole-source, five-year Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract, with a provision for a six-month extension in accordance with FAR 52.217-8, to Mercury Systems, Inc., CAGE Code 096Y5, located at 2665 Gulf Breeze Pkwy, Gulf Breeze, FL 32563. The Government projects contract award for December 2026. The Government requires the procurement of a Modernized Airborne Radio Control Head (MARCH) / Control Head Unit (CHU) solution to provide form, fit, function, and interface (F3I) cockpit radio control for the Air-to-Ground Networking Radio (AGNR) System and to replace the obsolete C-12601 Control Indicator (CI) within the AN/ARC-231A Radio Set across Army tactical rotorcraft (UH-60M/V Black Hawk, CH-47F Chinook, AH-64D/E Apache), designated fixed-wing aircraft, and unmanned aircraft systems (UAS). This effort will procure commercial-derivative Communication Management Units (CMUs), Mercury Systems ACM-9000 series hardware, specifically ACM-9544 CHUs and ACM-9443J CIs. The scope also encompasses airworthiness certification data and artifacts, proprietary operating system and runtime software licenses, and modernized MARCH engineering design, systems integration, and qualification testing services. This acquisition is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1 and RFO 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), which authorizes contracting other than full and open competition when there is only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Mercury Systems, Inc. is the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and the sole owner of the proprietary hardware manufacturing data packages, circuit schematics, FPGA register configurations, and safety-critical software source code for the qualified ACM-9544 and ACM-9443J units. The Government does not possess licensing rights to this technical data, and any alternative vendor would require an estimated 18 to 30 months to redesign, environmentally qualify, and airworthiness certify a replacement system. A schedule slip of this duration is unacceptable as it directly conflicts with the required AGNR 3QFY27 system-level production timeline and the early 3QFY28 C-12601 delivery date, which would exhaust depot supply channels and lead to mission degradation of operational aircraft. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and is published for informational purposes only. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. All responsible sources may submit a bid, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Submissions must provide clear and convincing evidence that the respondent possesses an existing, environmentally qualified (MIL-STD-810H and MIL-STD-461G), airworthy F3I drop-in replacement capable of meeting the Government�s initial delivery requirement of 90 days after receipt of order (ARO) without introducing schedule risk or requiring structural airframe modifications. Responses must be submitted via email no later than 4:00 PM EST on 27 November 2026 to the Contracting Officer, Roxanne Barbaris at roxanne.barbaris.civ@army.mil, and the Contract Specialist, Jessica Lefever, at jessica.d.lefever.civ@army.mil. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted, and the Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing submissions.

title: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES
description: DEFENSE LOGISTICS AGENCY (DLA) TROOP SUPPORT CLOTHING AND TEXTILES DIRECTORATE � PHILADELPHIA, PA REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) & SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Whole-of-Government Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS) & Commercial eMarketplace Platform FEDERAL MARKET RESEARCH NOTICE (FAR 15.201(e) & FAR Part 10): This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research, planning, and information-gathering purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. The Government is seeking broad industry input on commercial capabilities, architectural options, and market readiness. Responses are strictly voluntary; the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting responses to this notice. 1. Executive Summary & Purpose of Inquiry The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Troop Support Clothing and Textiles (C&T) Directorate is conducting market research to explore commercial software solutions, digital eMarketplace architectures, and industry best practices for deploying a next-generation Web-Based Ordering System (WBOS). DLA�s Troop Support C&T organization serves as the Federal Government�s primary enterprise manager for military clothing and textiles, working extensively with domestic industry. DLA is currently assessing the expansion of this shared-services procurement model to serve civilian Whole-of-Government (WOG) partner agencies, including the Department of the Interior (DOI), Department of Justice (DOJ), Department of Transportation (DOT), Department of State (DOS), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The primary objective of this RFI is to engage commercial e-commerce developers, SaaS providers, systems integrators, and domestic textile industry stakeholders. DLA seeks to understand what commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) capabilities exist today, how commercial technology can resolve complex federal supply chain and fiscal integration challenges, and what industry recommendations DLA should incorporate into its upcoming acquisition strategy. DLA is committed to adopting commercial best practices and avoiding custom development wherever commercial platforms can satisfy or be adapted to meet mission requirements. 2. Administrative Overview & Acquisition Milestones Market Research Parameter: Information & Acquisition Guidance Document Identifier: DLA-RFI-CT-2027-WBOS-MKTRES Anticipated Acquisition Approach: Commercial Solutions Opening (10 U.S.C. � 3458) / Commercial Acquisition (FAR Part 12 / Agile Authorities) Primary NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services (Small Business Size Standard: $34.0M) Secondary NAICS Codes: 518210 - Data Processing, Hosting, and Related Services ($40.0M), 541519 - Other Computer Related Services ($34.0M) Product Service Code (PSC): DA01 - IT and Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Software RFI Issuance Date: Friday, October 30, 2026 Industry Questions & Clarifications Due: Friday, November 06, 2026, at 16:00 EST Government Formal Q&A Responses Posted: Friday, November 20, 2026 RFI Capability Response Deadline: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 16:00 EST Anticipated Pre-Solicitation Industry Day: December 2, 2026 (Virtual) Primary Contract Specialist: Courtney Hunter, Contract Specialist, DLA Troop Support C&T (Courtney.Hunter@dla.mil) Primary Contracting Officer: Ryan Zarkowski, Individual Protection and Commercial Solutions Division Chief, DLA Troop Support (Ryan.Zarkowski@dla.mil) Submission Channel: Electronic submission via email to Government POCs (Subject: 'WBOS RFI Response - [Company Name]') 3. Mission Needs & Strategic Challenges The contemplated capability would enable Government-approved vendors to list and maintain Government-approved catalogs; enable authorized agency personnel to purchase authorized items; apply agency-specific eligibility, entitlement/allowance, item-authorization, approval, and management-control rules; support authorized payment methods; and provide auditable transaction, fulfillment, and program-management information. To modernize uniform procurement across DoD and civilian partner agencies, any future solution must address several interrelated operational and regulatory challenges. Rather than dictating prescriptive technical designs, DLA outlines the desired functional outcomes below to invite innovative, industry-driven solutions: Operational Domain: The Operational Challenge / Desired Outcome Commercial Marketplace & User Experience: Deliver a modern, consumer-grade multi-tenant e-commerce experience with sub-second catalog search, faceted filtering, mobile responsiveness, and intuitive uniform selection, while supporting distinct tenant agency branding (DoD, DOI, DOJ, DOT, DOS, DHS) and role-based permissions. Domestic Provenance & Supply Chain Integrity: Because DLA operates as a central procurement hub utilizing the Defense Working Capital Fund (DWCF), end-items transacted through DLA are subject to 100% domestic sourcing requirements under the Berry Amendment (10 U.S.C. � 4862). DLA requires automated mechanisms to verify domestic origin down to the raw material/mill level, screen supply chains for forced labor or prohibited foreign entities, and prevent unverified items from being purchased. Statutory Competition & Micro-Purchases: In a multi-vendor marketplace environment, transactions must respect federal competition mandates (such as CICA and simplified acquisition thresholds). The Government seeks automated, user-friendly marketplace workflows that promote fair competition, facilitate dynamic quoting between micro-purchase thresholds ($15k) and simplified acquisition threshold ($350k), and prevent improper order splitting without creating administrative bottlenecks. Uniform Customization & Value-Added Logistics: Civilian law enforcement and military personnel require customized uniforms (e.g., branch tapes, badges, department patches, embroidery, reflective safety trims, and tailored sizing). The system must support interactive customization, dimensionally accurate digital proofing, supervisor approvals, and tracking of value-added tailoring services while ensuring all component materials remain compliant. Interagency Accounting & Fiscal Guardrails: The system must handle interagency funding across diverse partner departments without risking Antideficiency Act (ADA) violations. This includes integrating with federal financial frameworks (such as Treasury G-Invoicing Form 7600A/B), managing annual individual officer uniform allowances (5 U.S.C. � 5901), supporting multi-payment split tender (allowance + GPC + personal card overages), and reconciling DLA cost-recovery surcharges without contractor fee retention. Cybersecurity & Enterprise Interoperability: The platform will process sensitive federal uniform requisitions, military supply chain data, and law enforcement personnel information. It must meet high federal cybersecurity baselines (such as FedRAMP and DoD Cloud Computing Security Requirements), support CAC/PIV single sign-on, and interface with federal backbones such as DLA Enterprise Business System (EBS/SAP), PIEE/WAWF, and SAM.gov. Training & Performance Tracking: Provide general user training, program manager training, etc. Implement all necessary work and time management control processes to ensure timely accurate accomplishment of work requirements as well as to permit tracking work in progress. 4. Areas of Inquiry & Market Research Questionnaire Industry respondents are invited to address the following questions. Offerors may respond to all or selected inquiry areas based on their core competencies and commercial experience. 4.1 Pillar 1: Market Position & Differentiation Question 1.1 (Core Competencies): Outline your primary services and expertise, such as previous projects in a similar scope, or any COTS options you currently off

title: Program Analysis and Control (PAAC V) Bridge
description: NASA/GSFC intends to extend the period of performance for a period of six (6) months and increase the maximum ordering value of Contract 80GSFC25D0003, Program Analysis and Control (PAAC V) Bridge with ASRC Federal System Solutions (AFSS). The PAAC V Bridge contract provides accounting, planning and scheduling/earned value management, documentation management, configuration management and security compliance. The place of performance for PAAC V Bridge is the NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) Facilities and Installations, NASA Headquarters (HQ), Langley Research Center, and other NASA Centers, as needed. NASA/GSFC intends to extend the ordering period for six (6) additional months from December 1, 2026, to May 31, 2027, and increase the maximum ordering value of the PAAC V Bridge contract to ensure uninterrupted support until the follow-on competitive contract is awarded and contract transition is completed. The proposed increase of $20.24M will revise the contract maximum ordering value from $180,000,000 to $200,240,000. This procurement action is being conducted on a sole source basis in accordance with FAR 6.302-1 and 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1). As the incumbent contractor, AFSS is uniquely qualified to provide the services required. AFSS is considered the only contractor that can meet GSFC�s needs, without disruption to current programs and services, given the short amount of time remaining under the current contract. These services function as integral parts of all the aforementioned NASA missions. The skills required to support such critical missions and milestones cannot be readily replaced. Award to any other source for this period would delay NASA/GSFC�s missions. The government does not intend to acquire a commercial item using FAR Part 12. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Cynthia White at Cynthia.L.White@nasa.gov no later than 4:30pm local time on November 27, 2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based on responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the government. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. NASA Clause 1852.215-84 Ombudsman is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf

Θα συνδέει τον αυτοκινητόδρομο Λευκωσίας-Κοκκινοτριμιθιάς με τον αυτοκινητόδρομο Αστρομερίτη-Ευρύχου και θα διέρχεται νότια των χωριών Ακακίου, Περιστερώνας και Αστρομερίτη. Η τυπική διατομή περιλαμβάνει 4 λωρίδες κυκλοφορίας 3,5 μ έκαστη με κεντρική νησίδα και με ασφαλτοστρωμένα ερείσματα εκατέρωθεν, πλάτους 3,0 μ. Οι κατασκευαστικές εργασίες, μεταξύ άλλων περιλαμβάνουν 4 ανισόπεδους κόμβους, τη συμπλήρωση ενός υφιστάμενου ανισόπεδου κόμβου, χωματουργικές και ασφαλτικές εργασίες, εργασίες αποχέτευσης ομβρίων περιλαμβανομένων εργασιών κατασκευής κλειστού συστήματος απορροής ομβρίων οδοστρώματος, τροποποιήσεις υφιστάμενων Υπηρεσιών, εγκαταστάσεις νέων Υπηρεσιών, εγκατάσταση οδικού φωτισμού, κοιλαδογέφυρες, υπέργειες και υπόγειες διαβάσεις, ορθογωνικούς οχετούς και τοίχους αντιστήριξης. description: Η παρούσα μελέτη αφορά την μίσθωση μηχανημάτων και φορτηγών, με την μορφή έξι (6) ομάδων, ως εξής: 1η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>120 ΗΡ) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 2η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>120 ΗΡ) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 3η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από έναν (1) ερπυστριοφόρο υδραυλικό εκσκαφέα (>50 ΗΡ έως 120 HP) και ένα (1) φορτηγό ανατρεπόμενο, 4η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα, 5η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα, 6η ομάδα αποτελούμενη από δύο (2) ερπυστριοφόρους υδραυλικούς εκσκαφείς (>120 ΗΡ) και δύο (2) φορτηγά ανατρεπόμενα. Συγκεκριμένα τα μισθωμένα μηχανήματα με τη μορφή ομάδων – συνεργείων, θα χρησιμοποιηθούν για τον καθαρισμό κοίτης και συγκεκριμένα την απομάκρυνση απορριμμάτων και μπαζών, για απομάκρυνση βλάστησης (καλαμιών, θάμνων, δέντρων), για άρση λοιπών εμποδίων (ξεροί κορμοί, κ.λπ.), για διαμόρφωση πρανών για την αποφυγή καταπτώσεων, για φόρτωση και μεταφορά προϊόντων καθαρισμού σε κατάλληλους χώρους καθώς και για τοπικές αποκαταστάσεις ζημιών σε αναχώματα. Οι ως άνω περιγραφόμενες εργασίες θα πραγματοποιηθούν με απώτερο σκοπό την ελεύθερη απορροή των υδάτων σε ρέματα, υδατορέματα, χειμάρρους και ποταμούς στα γεωγραφικά όρια της Περιφερειακής Ενότητας Ροδόπης, τα οποία θα υποδειχτούν από την Υπηρεσία μας και είναι συγκεκριμένα τα παρακάτω δεκαέξι (16) σημεία επέμβασης: Ρέμα Δυτικά Οικισμού Αμαξάδων, Ρέμα Ανατολικά Οικισμού Αμαξάδων ή Αμυγδαλόρεμα, Ρέμα Ασκητών, Ρέμα Βοσβόζη ή Ασπρόρεμα, Ρέμα Γλυφάδας 1, Ρέμα Γλυφάδας 2, Ρέμα Καλλυντηρίου, Ρέμα Μαυρομματίου 1, Ρέμα Μαυρομματίου 2, Ρέμα Παγουρίων, Ρέμα Πανεπιστημιούπολης, Ρέμα Παραδημής ή Χηνόρεμα, Ρέμα Πελαγίας, Ρέμα Πλατανίτη, Ρέμα Πλησίον Ηφαίστου, Ρέμα Φαναρίου. Οι ώρες εργασίας (διάρκεια μίσθωσης) της κάθε ομάδας είναι: ΟΜΑΔΑ ΩΡΕΣ ΜΙΣΘΩΣΗΣ 1η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 2η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 3η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1581,7672 4η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1000 5η ΟΜΑΔΑ 1300 6η ΟΜΑΔΑ 2000 Οι ώρες εργασίας του κάθε συνεργείου, υπολογίζονται ότι θα εξαντληθούν συνεχόμενα ή τμηματικά, σε χρονική διάρκεια είκοσι τεσσάρων (24) μηνών, όπως αναλυτικότερα περιγράφεται στη Τεχνική Περιγραφή και Προϋπολογισμό της παροχής υπηρεσίας, προϋπολογισμού 2.000.000,00 € συμπεριλαμβανομένου Φ.Π.Α.

title: Presolicitation Notice for V-22/H-53 Forward Looking-Infrared Performance Based Logistics Requirements Contract.
description: NAVSUP Weapon Systems Support (NAVSUP WSS) Philadelphia plans to award a Performance Based Logistics (PBL) requirements contract in support of the Forward-looking Infrared (FLIR) on the V-22 aircraft and CH-53 helicopter. This requirement includes repair, replacement of assets, warehousing, issuance of assets in response to requisitions in accordance with availability requirements, supply chain management, configuration management, and obsolescence management. The Government intends to contract on a sole source basis with Raytheon Company (CAGE code 96214) located in McKinney, TX. The resultant PBL contract will include one 5-year base period and no option period. The contract will include PBL support of 12 NSNs which are listed in the attached document. Justification for Sole Source Acquisition is based upon the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, only one or a limited number of responsible sources and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Absent interest/approval of additional sources, the Government intends to solicit Raytheon Company. Raytheon Company is the only source capable of providing integrated logistics support for the entire scope of necessary performance requirements related to repair, manufacturing, availability, engineering sustainment, obsolescence management, and required forecasting. NAVSUP WSS does not own rights to drawings. Drawings cannot be obtained, nor is it possible to draft adequate specifications for them to facilitate competition at this time. The subject items require Government source approval prior to contract award, as the items are flight critical and/or the technical data available has not been determined adequate to support repair via full and open competition. Only the Raytheon Company will be solicited. The time required for approval of a new source is normally such that an award cannot be delayed pending approval of a new source. If you are not an approved source you must submit, together with your proposal, the information detailed in the NAVSUP WSS Source Approval Information Brochure for repair. A Source Approval Request (SAR) brochure is available upon request. If your request for source approval is currently being evaluated at NAVSUP WSS submit with your offer a copy of the cover letter which forwarded your request for source approval. Offers received which fail to provide all data required by the Source Approval Brochure or document previous submission of all data required by the Source Approval Brochure will not be considered for award under this solicitation. Please note, if evaluation of a source approval request submitted hereunder cannot be processed in time and/or approval requirements preclude the ability to obtain subject items in time to meet Government requirements, award of the subject requirement may continue based on Fleet support needs. Based upon market research, the Government is not using the policies contained in FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, in its solicitation for the described supplies or services. However, interested persons may identify to the contracting officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item within 15 days of this notice. For information or questions regarding this notice, please contact Olga Maksimchuk by e-mail Olga.Maksimchuk.civ@us.navy.mil.
